page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.13xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 52 dedicated physical cores and 52 vCPUs at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, which translates to a resource density of 1.85 GB of memory per core. It does not feature any local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average multi-core performance, as shown by its stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 45505.98 and Geekbench multi-core score of 11386.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scores falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a throughput of 190.74 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 40.39 million operations per second, consistently rank in the middle 50%.

Given its high core count relative to memory capacity, the ecs.c6e.13xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for highly parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The lack of local NVMe SSDs and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, making it unsuitable for local database caching or hardware-accelerated machine learning. It is best suited for multi-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and parallelized CPU-bound workloads.
